about: Generated by program-instructions/scripts/program-facts.cjs from the pack inputs files named in provenance; do not edit by hand. For each program on its platform and bridge: the measured facts a written text says, what it never says, and the words a text must and must not hold.

facts: Text Editor edits plain text files. `computer.open` with app org.gnome.texteditor starts it; `computer.app` with "action": "apps" lists its open windows.
A snapshot holds the whole document as one element with the role text box, editable, whose value is the document's text.
To change the document, type into that element: mode replace sets the whole text, insert puts the text at `at`, append adds it at the end.

The answer's `after` is what the document holds when read again, and `verified` says whether that is what was asked for. When verified is false, read a new snapshot before anything else; do not repeat the type.
A change is undone with "action": "undo", which writes the earlier text back only while the document still holds what was written; otherwise "action": "restore" opens the copy saved before it.

Text Editor declares no verbs: opening, saving, searching and replacing files are not done through invoke, which answers "I can't do <verb> in Text Editor yet." The person saves the file in Text Editor.
A one-line box in Text Editor (such as its search box) is not typed into: "Orbit cannot tell whether this box is a password field, so it does not type into it".
never: A menu path, a key or a key combination as something Jarvis does (no Ctrl+S, no File menu).
That Jarvis saves, opens or searches files in Text Editor.
Any declared verb for Text Editor (insert-paragraph, format-text, save-document and the rest belong to LibreOffice).
Any tool other than computer.app and computer.open.

facts: `computer.open` with app org.gnome.terminal opens a Terminal window; `computer.app` with "action": "apps" lists its windows.
A snapshot reads the lines shown in the terminal as one element with the role terminal; the empty rows below the last line are empty lines. Only what is shown is read.

Nothing is typed into the terminal: "action": "type" is refused with "Terminal did not do that: This needs the mouse and keyboard." and nothing reaches the program running in it. Do not repeat it; tell the person the terminal takes typing only from the keyboard.
Terminal declares no verbs; invoke answers "I can't do <verb> in Terminal yet."
never: A command for Jarvis to type into the terminal, or any shell command presented as something Jarvis runs there.
A key or key combination as something Jarvis does.
That the terminal's text can be changed through computer.app.
Any tool other than computer.app and computer.open.

facts: Two ways in, told apart by the snapshot: with Orbit's LibreOffice add-on connected, `part` is "whole" and the reading holds every paragraph and table; without it, `part` is "visible" and `shown` says "the paragraphs shown on the screen".

With the add-on: the declared verbs insert-paragraph, add-section, replace-text, delete-paragraph, format-text, find-replace and the file verbs recent-documents, open-document, new-document, save-document, export-document, each through "action": "invoke", each one step on LibreOffice's own Undo.

With the add-on (1.2.3 and later), replace-text and find-replace change only the matched text, as without it: the text around it keeps its bold, italic and font, the new text takes the formatting of the text it replaces, a match in more than one formatting is refused and nothing changes, and the answer carries `verified` from reading back the text and each character's formatting. find-replace with the add-on reaches the whole document (tables left out), and `"all": false` changes only the first match; the whole change is one named step on LibreOffice's Undo. A line ending in the new text is a line break inside that paragraph, with or without the add-on; add paragraphs with insert-paragraph.

Without the add-on: insert-paragraph and add-section add plain paragraphs only; a heading, a font size, or bold, italic or underline inside insert-paragraph or replace-text is refused in words naming the add-on ("... needs the LibreOffice add-on: install it in Orbit Settings, Bound Apps (Install the LibreOffice add-on)"), and nothing changes.

Without the add-on: format-text sets bold, italic or underline on a paragraph (`ref`) or a text (`find`) and is checked in the text's own attributes; when the format does not read back it is refused and nothing is claimed.

Without the add-on: replace-text (with `find`) and find-replace change only the matched text. The text around it keeps its bold, italic and font, and the new text takes the formatting of the text it replaces (a bold word replaced stays bold). The answer's `verified` is true only when both the text and that formatting read back as expected.

Without the add-on: a match that is in more than one formatting (part bold, part plain) is refused and nothing changes: "'<text>' is in more than one formatting ('<part>' | '<part>'), so its new text could keep only one of them; nothing changed. Replace each part on its own." Replace each part with its own replace-text.

Without the add-on: replace-text without `find` replaces the paragraph's whole text (by `ref`, else the first paragraph shown); the new text takes the formatting the paragraph ends with. With a `find` the paragraph named by `ref` does not hold, it is refused and nothing changes.

Without the add-on: find-replace reaches only the paragraphs shown on the screen, changes at most 10 places at once (20 when the replacement is empty), is refused when the paragraphs shown hold none, and answers the touched paragraphs before and as read back. One "action": "undo" with its group takes the whole change away. Searching the whole document in one step needs the add-on.
Without the add-on: delete-paragraph leaves the paragraph empty in place; the file verbs are refused.
Every edit's answer carries `after` as read back and `verified`; when verified is false, read a new snapshot before anything else.
An edit is undone with "action": "undo" naming the answer's undo `how` and `group`.
never: That a heading, a font size or a paragraph style can be set without the add-on.
That replace-text or find-replace drop the formatting of the paragraph they change, with or without the add-on (both did in Orbit 0.7.19 with add-on 1.2.2; since kernel 1cefa139 neither does).
A menu path, a key or a key combination as something Jarvis does (the shipped guide names menus only as where the person finds things).
Anything the shipped guide says differently about the add-on's verbs.
Any tool other than computer.app and computer.open.

A list box cannot be chosen from ("that element cannot be selected"), a password field is never typed into, and scroll is refused because Chrome publishes no scroll bar.
Act only in a Chrome window that is in front: a window covered by another runs no press and does not update what it shows until it is uncovered.
never: That the person must start Chrome with a flag or change a desktop setting: Orbit starts it readable when it opens it.
That Jarvis types into a page field, the address bar or a search box in Chrome.
That Jarvis chooses an option in a list box.
A menu path, a key or a key combination as something Jarvis does.

facts: A snapshot holds the tab in front as one element with the role document text, labelled "Text editor", editable, whose value is that tab's text; each tab is a page tab whose name carries its document name and Modified or Unmodified.
A new tab is opened with "action": "press" on the push button "Add New Tab". Read a new snapshot after it: the new tab is in front, named Untitled, with an empty Text editor.
To write, "action": "type" into the Text editor element: mode replace sets the tab's whole text, append adds the text at the end, insert puts it at `at`.

Each tab has its own Text editor element, and a type goes into the element its snapshot's ref names, even when another tab is in front. To work in another tab, "action": "select" that tab, read a new snapshot and use the Text editor it shows.

The answer's `after` is what the element holds when read again, and `verified` says whether that is what was asked for. When Orbit could not read it back, the type is refused with "Orbit sent the text but could not read it back, so what is there now is not verified. Read a new snapshot before anything else." The text was sent once: do not repeat the type.

A change is undone with "action": "undo", which writes the earlier text back only while the element still holds what was written. A tab never saved has no copy, so there is nothing for "action": "restore" to open for it.
A minimized Notepad is shown again, without being brought to the front, before a snapshot or an act; the reading's `shown` then says "the window was minimized and Orbit showed it again first".
Notepad declares no verbs: opening, saving and searching files are not done through invoke, which answers "I can't do <verb> in Notepad yet." The person saves the file in Notepad.
A window of a program that runs as administrator is never read or acted in: the answer says "it runs as administrator, and Orbit reads only programs that run with its own rights".
never: A menu path, a key or a key combination as something Jarvis does (no Ctrl+S, no Ctrl+T, no File menu).
That Jarvis saves, opens or searches files in Notepad.

facts: A snapshot reads the whole document (`part` is "whole"): one element with the role document text, named after the document, whose value is the document's text.

Word declares the edit verbs insert-paragraph, add-section, replace-text, delete-paragraph, format-text and find-replace, each run with "action": "invoke" and the same inputs as in LibreOffice Writer. Orbit runs each through Word's own object model as one step on Word's own Undo; Word is not brought to the front and no key is sent.

format-text sets bold, italic, underline or a font size on the text found or on a paragraph, and a heading level on a paragraph. insert-paragraph adds paragraphs at the end, at the start, or before or after a paragraph; add-section's title is a level 2 heading unless a level is given.

replace-text replaces the text found, or the whole paragraph named by `ref`, and the rest of the paragraph keeps its format. find-replace changes every occurrence, or only the first with "all": false, and leaves paragraphs inside tables alone. A text that is nowhere is refused: "could not find '<text>' in the document".
Every edit's answer carries `after` as read back from the document, and `verified`; when verified is false, read a new snapshot before anything else.

An edit is undone with "action": "undo" naming the answer's undo `how` and `group`. Word's own Undo takes it back only while the document's text is what that edit left; otherwise nothing is undone and the answer says so.

"action": "type" on the document element can append, or insert at `at`. Replacing the whole text of a document that has text is refused: "Replacing the whole text of a Word document would drop its formatting. Use replace-text, insert-paragraph, delete-paragraph, format-text or find-replace, or type with append or insert." A type is not on Word's Undo, so undoing one offers the copy instead.

Opening, saving and exporting files are not Word verbs: invoke answers "I can't do <verb> in Word yet." and the person opens and saves files in Word. The copy kept before an edit is the file as last saved; a document never saved has none.
A paragraph inside a table and a protected document are refused in words and nothing changes. A window that runs as administrator is never read or acted in.
never: A menu path, a ribbon button, a key or a key combination as something Jarvis does (no Ctrl+B, no Ctrl+Z).
That Jarvis opens, saves or exports a Word document, or any file verb for Word.
That "action": "type" with mode replace replaces the text of a document that already has text.
That a spreadsheet verb (set-cells, read-range and the rest) works in Word.
Any tool other than computer.app and computer.open.

facts: Excel declares the spreadsheet verbs read-range, set-cells, format-cells, find-replace, sort-range, filter-range, manage-sheet, create-pivot-table and add-chart, each run with "action": "invoke" and the same inputs as in LibreOffice Calc. Orbit runs each through Excel's own object model; Excel is not brought to the front and no key is sent.

Read cells with read-range: each cell of a range on the sheet in front, or on one named, with what it shows and its formula, at most 2,000 cells at once ("that range holds <n> cells; read at most 2000 at once"). A sheet that is not there is refused ("there is no sheet named <name>").

Write cells with set-cells, by address: a text that starts with = is a formula, one that reads as a number is a number, an empty one clears the cell, and anything else stays text (1/2 and TRUE stay texts). A formula Excel does not take is refused, and the cells written before it are put back.

format-cells sets bold, italic, underline, a font size, a number format (currency, percent or a pattern), fill and font colour, and a column width or auto-fit. find-replace changes every match on the sheet in any case and answers how many; a text that is nowhere is refused ("could not find '<text>' in sheet <name>").

sort-range orders a range's rows by one column (a header, column letters or a number) and keeps the header row; filter-range shows or hides the rows below the first by one column's cell, and "clear": true shows every row; manage-sheet adds, renames, shows or deletes a sheet, and deletes only a sheet that holds nothing.

create-pivot-table makes a native PivotTable from `sourceRange` (default A1:D13; its first row names the fields) at `targetCell` (default F1) on `targetSheet` (else `sheet`): `rowFields` down the rows (default the first column), optional `columnFields` across, `dataFields` by header, and `function` SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MAX or MIN (any other is SUM). Its name is `name`, else JarvisPivot, then JarvisPivot2 and on.

A pivot table is never moved or written over anything: Orbit lays it out on a sheet it adds and deletes again, then builds it only where every cell it covered on the way is empty and off its own source (an empty table covers 18 rows by 3 columns, so F1 needs F1:H18 empty). Refused in words, leaving nothing behind: a place inside its source or over cells that hold something (the answer names the cells), a name the sheet already has, a source column without a header, a sheet that is not there.

A pivot table is made only while the bound workbook is the one in front in Excel. Otherwise it is refused with `not-active` before anything changes, and the person clicks that workbook's window in Excel and asks again; Orbit does not switch Excel's workbooks.

add-chart inserts a native chart over `sourceRange` (or `range`; default A1:D13) on `sheet`: the first row names the series and the first column holds the categories. `chartType` is column (the default), bar, line, pie, area or scatter, and any other is drawn as column; it has a title only when `title` is given; its name is `name`, else JarvisChart or the next free name. A range of only a header row is refused, and so is a name the sheet already has.
Every written cell, pivot table and chart is read back from Excel, and the answer carries `verified`; when verified is false, read the range again before anything else.

An edit is undone with "action": "undo" naming the answer's undo `how` and `group`: Orbit puts back what its cells held only while every one still holds what the edit left, and deletes a pivot table or chart it made only while that still reads exactly as made (one changed in Excel is kept and the undo refused). Otherwise nothing is put back. Excel's own Undo does not take these edits back, and a format-cells is not undone in place.

Opening or saving workbooks are not Excel verbs: invoke answers "I can't do <verb> in Excel yet." A protected sheet is refused, and so is a busy Excel (a cell being edited, or a dialog open). Typing into the grid with "action": "type" was not measured; cells are written with set-cells.
never: A menu path, a ribbon button, a key or a key combination as something Jarvis does (no Ctrl+Z).
That Jarvis opens, saves or exports a workbook, or any file verb for Excel.
That Excel's own Undo takes back an edit Jarvis made.
That a pivot table is moved or placed over cells that hold something, or that a pivot table or chart replaces one of the same name.
That Jarvis switches Excel's workbooks or brings Excel to the front to make a pivot table.
A chart type other than column, bar, line, pie, area or scatter.
That a text-document verb (insert-paragraph, format-text and the rest) works in Excel.
Any tool other than computer.app and computer.open.

facts: PowerPoint declares the slide verbs add-slide, set-slide-text, replace-text, format-text, delete-slide and move-slide, each run with "action": "invoke" and its inputs. Orbit runs each through PowerPoint's own object model as one step on PowerPoint's own undo list; PowerPoint is not brought to the front and no key is sent. Slides are numbered from 1, as PowerPoint numbers them.

add-slide adds a slide at the end, or at the `start`, or `after` or `before` slide `slide` (`position`), with `title` and `body` (a paragraph per line) in the layout's placeholders. `layout` is title, title-and-content (the default), section-header, two-content, title-only or blank. A layout without the placeholder asked for is refused ("the blank layout has no title placeholder"), and so is a place past the last slide; neither leaves a slide.

set-slide-text replaces the text of slide `slide`'s title placeholder with `title`, of its body placeholder with `body`, or both; a placeholder not asked for keeps its text. A slide without the placeholder asked for is refused ("slide <n> has no title placeholder") and nothing changes.

replace-text replaces every occurrence of `find`, in exact case, with `replace` on every slide, or only on slide `slide`, and answers how many it replaced (`count`). A text that is nowhere is refused: "could not find '<text>' in the presentation". Text in tables, groups, charts and notes is not changed.

format-text makes slide `slide`'s title or body placeholder (`target`), or every occurrence of `find` on that slide, `bold`, `italic` or `underline` (true or false) and/or `fontSize` points. A `find` that is not on the slide is refused: "could not find '<text>' on slide <n>".
delete-slide deletes slide `slide`; move-slide moves slide `slide` so that it becomes slide `to`. A move to the number the slide already has is refused and changes nothing.
Every edit's answer is read back from the presentation and carries `before`, `after` and `verified`; when verified is false, read a new snapshot before anything else.

An edit is undone with "action": "undo" naming the answer's undo `how` and `group`. Orbit runs PowerPoint's own Undo only while the presentation reads exactly as that edit left it and its window is the one PowerPoint has active; Orbit never switches PowerPoint's windows. An edit already undone, or one the presentation changed after, is refused and nothing is undone. When PowerPoint's Undo takes another change on top of the edit instead, Orbit puts that change back with Redo and refuses the undo.

Opening, saving and exporting presentations are not PowerPoint verbs: invoke answers "I can't do <verb> in <program> yet.", and the person opens and saves files in PowerPoint. A read-only or final presentation and a busy PowerPoint (a dialog open) are refused in words. Slide text is written with add-slide and set-slide-text; typing into a slide with "action": "type" was not measured.
never: A menu path, a ribbon button, a key or a key combination as something Jarvis does (no Ctrl+M, no Ctrl+Z).
That Jarvis opens, saves or exports a presentation, or any file verb for PowerPoint.
A slide verb other than the six declared ids: new-slide and insert-slide are not declared names.
That replace-text or format-text changes text in tables, groups, charts or speaker notes.
That a text-document or spreadsheet verb (insert-paragraph, set-cells and the rest) works in PowerPoint.
Any tool other than computer.app and computer.open.

facts: Godot Engine is the Godot 4 editor, and Jarvis works in it only through Orbit's add-on in the open project. With the add-on a snapshot has `part` "whole" and reads the project, its open scenes, the edited scene's node tree (one line per node with its type and facts such as position, script, text, texture or instance of), the selection, whether the game runs, the project's input actions, its files and the scripts open. The document is the project, by its name.

Without the add-on the snapshot is refused with "Orbit's Godot add-on is not running in this project. Turn it on in Orbit Settings, Bound Apps, Godot Engine, Orbit's add-on in this project" and the window declares no verbs.

Every change is a declared verb through "action": "invoke": add-node, set-property, create-script, edit-script, rename-node, move-node, delete-node, add-input-action, instance-scene and import-asset. Each is one named step on Godot's own undo list ("Jarvis: <what> (#tag)"), which the person's own undo in Godot also undoes. A node is named by its path from the snapshot, such as Main/Player.

A node is never typed into, pressed or selected: a type, press or select of a node is refused with "Jarvis changes Godot through its declared actions (set-property, rename-node and the others)". Change a node only with its verbs.

set-property sets `property` of `node` in the property's own type: a number, true or false, text, [x, y] or "Vector2(1, 2)" for a position, "#ff8800" for a colour, a res:// path for a resource. The answer's `verified` says whether the property reads back as asked.

create-script writes a new res://….gd from `code` and attaches it to `node`; code that does not compile is refused with Godot's own words and nothing is written, and a script that would run inside the editor (@tool, EditorPlugin, EditorScript) is refused. edit-script changes a script in Godot's script editor: `text` is the whole new script, or `find` and `replace`. Nothing under res://addons/ or res://.godot/ is changed.

To try the game: run-scene (the edited scene by default, "main" for the main scene, or a res:// scene), then game-output for what it printed with its errors and warnings, each with the script line it came from (such as res://player.gd:6), then stop-scene. Godot saves the scenes before it runs them when its own setting says so.

Scenes and files are acts, not undo steps: open-scene, new-scene (a res://….tscn that does not exist yet, with root_type such as Node2D or Node3D), save-scene (with `as` for a new file). add-input-action adds keys such as ["Space", "W"] to an input action and saves project.godot. instance-scene adds another scene; import-asset adds a .png, .jpg, .webp, .svg, .glb or .gltf already in the project folder, a picture as a Sprite2D and a model as an instance.

"action": "undo" undoes one change, only while it is the newest change on Godot's undo list; a change with newer ones on top is refused and nothing is undone, so undo the newest first. Orbit keeps no copy of a Godot project, so "action": "restore" has nothing to open.
show-view puts the edited scene's 2D or 3D view (`what` "editor", "2d" or "3d") or the running game (`what` "game") in front of the screen for a look; a snapshot itself carries no picture.
never: A menu path, a key or a key combination as something Jarvis does (no Ctrl+S, no Ctrl+Z, no Scene menu).
That Jarvis types into, presses or selects a node or a field of the Godot editor.
That Jarvis changes files under res://addons/ or res://.godot/, or writes @tool scripts or editor plugins.
That the add-on or a snapshot sends a picture or a screenshot.
A verb other than Godot's seventeen (no insert-paragraph, save-document or export-document), and any tool other than computer.app and computer.open.

facts: A snapshot ("action": "snapshot") reads the whole open .blend through Orbit's Blender add-on: a File line (its name, whether it has unsaved changes, Blender's version, the mode), a Scene line per scene, an Object line per object (type, location, rotation in degrees, scale, mesh vertex and face counts, parent, modifiers, materials), a Material line per material (base color as #RRGGBB, metallic, roughness, who uses it) and the Selection with the active object.

Blender is never typed into, pressed or selected: every change is "action": "invoke" with a declared verb and its inputs, the object named by its name in object (the active object when none is named). Each object of a snapshot is an element with the role object and is read only.

Each edit is one named step on Blender's own undo list, "Jarvis: <what> (#tag)", so the person's Ctrl+Z in Blender takes it back. "action": "undo" with the change takes it back with Blender's own Undo only while it is Blender's latest step; when other changes came after it, the answer says so and nothing is undone.

Rotation is in degrees, location in Blender units, and scale is one number or [x, y, z]. transform-object with relative: true adds to the location and rotation and multiplies the scale. add-primitive makes a cube, plane, uv-sphere, ico-sphere, cylinder, cone, torus, monkey, circle or grid with UVs, at the 3D cursor unless location is given, and selects it.

set-material-color takes color as "#RRGGBB", as Blender's color picker shows it, or [r, g, b] from 0 to 1, with metallic and roughness from 0 to 1; an object with no material gets a new one. The snapshot's Material line then shows the color as #RRGGBB.

An edit Blender refuses changes nothing, and its words say why: an unknown object lists the objects there are, a modifier setting Blender does not have lists the settings it has, and a parent that would make a loop is refused.

Modifiers are named by Blender's types (SUBSURF, BEVEL, MIRROR, ARRAY, SOLIDIFY, DECIMATE, TRIANGULATE, WELD, BOOLEAN and the rest) and set by Blender's own property names, such as {"levels": 2}; apply-modifier applies one to the mesh, as a game engine needs it.
Blender is edited only in Object Mode: while the person is in Edit Mode or another mode, an edit is refused with words asking them to press Tab in Blender.

export-glb writes a glTF binary .glb into folder (a path, or beside the .blend) of the whole scene, the listed objects or selectedOnly, modifiers applied, Y up. When the folder is inside a Godot project, the answer gives the res:// path Godot imports it as; that is the hand-off to Godot.
save-file saves in place; a file never saved needs as (a file name, saved beside it or in Documents). Another file of that name is replaced only with overwrite: true.

run-python follows the person's two Python switches in Blender, which the snapshot's Python snippets line states: off, it is refused; on and asking (the default), call it without confirmed, put the answer's question to the person, and call again with confirmed: true only after their yes; on without asking, it runs at once. A scheduled turn never runs Python, and a snippet stops after five seconds.

viewport-screenshot saves a PNG of the 3D viewport in Orbit's folder and answers in words what it shows: the view, where it looks from, the shading and which objects are in sight. The picture itself does not come back in the answer.
When Orbit's add-on is not connected in that Blender, Blender cannot be read and the answer says to install it in Orbit Settings, Bound Apps, Install the Blender add-on, then open Blender again.

edit-mesh takes operation (extrude, inset, bevel, loop-cut, subdivide, move, scale; never op) and faces: all, selected, a side such as "+z", the face numbers read-object lists, or {"facing": "+x", "near": [x, y, z]} for the one face on that side nearest a point. The new faces become selected, so the next edit can take "selected".
clean-mesh with operation decimate and budget brings a mesh to at most that many triangles; scene-stats counts triangles per object and says whether a budget holds.

A game character is made in order: uv-unwrap, texture-material (picture files), add-armature with rig humanoid and fit (Godot's humanoid bone names), skin-to-armature (the answer says how many vertices got weights), then one make-action per animation.
export-glb writes each action make-action made as its own animation and says what the .glb holds; Godot's AnimationPlayer then lists them by name.
import-model reads a .glb, .gltf, .fbx or .obj and says what arrived; bake-texture needs UVs and a material and saves a PNG at file, with its res:// path inside a Godot project.
never: A key, a menu path or a mouse step as something Jarvis does: the person's Ctrl+Z and Tab are theirs.
That Jarvis types into, presses or selects anything in Blender.
That run-python is called with confirmed: true before the person said yes in this conversation.
That the viewport picture comes back to Jarvis.
Any declared verb of another program (save-document, insert-paragraph, set-cells and the rest).
Any tool other than computer.app and computer.open.
That run-python runs in a scheduled turn, or without the person's yes while Blender asks before each snippet.

facts: With Orbit's VS Code extension connected, a snapshot reads the active file whole ("part" is "whole"; the shown line says "through Orbit's VS Code extension"): one element with the role document named after the file, whose value is the file's text, and a selection element while text is selected. Without the extension a snapshot reads only the visible window and declares no verbs: ask the person to press Install Orbit's extension in Visual Studio Code in Orbit Settings, Bound Apps; VS Code starts it at once, with no restart.

"action": "type" on the document element appends ("mode": "append"), inserts at a character ("mode": "insert" with "at") or replaces the whole file ("mode": "replace"); on the selection element it replaces the selected text. Each is one step on VS Code's own Undo, its answer carries "verified", and it is refused when the file changed since the snapshot. Nothing is saved until save-file.

The extension declares workspace, read-file, problems, find-in-files, open-file, edit-text, save-file, list-tasks, run-task, run-command, terminals and terminal-output, each run with "action": "invoke" and its inputs. Files are named by their path inside the workspace (such as src/app.js); a file outside the window's folders is refused. open-file makes a file the active one the next snapshot reads.

edit-text changes the active file or `path` as one WorkspaceEdit: `find` with `replace` changes one place (a text found more than once is refused unless `all` is true), `line` and `endLine` with `text` replace whole lines, and `text` with `at` (start, end or a line number) inserts. The answer carries the lines before and after and "verified".

An edit or a type is undone with "action": "undo" naming the answer's undo how and group: VS Code's own Undo while the change is still the last one in its file; after the person changed the file again, only the change's own text is written back, and when that text is gone the undo is refused and "action": "restore" opens the copy saved before the change.

run-command and run-task run something only when the person asked for that command or task in this conversation. An invoke without confirmed: true is refused with the question to put to the person ("Ask the person first: Run ...? ... Nothing was run."); only after they say yes is it sent again with confirmed: true. A command is one line and runs in a terminal named Jarvis the person sees; the answer carries its output and exit code (it waits at most 50 seconds). In a folder VS Code holds in Restricted Mode nothing runs, confirmed or not.

terminal-output reads what a terminal wrote since the extension started (commands VS Code's shell integration reports, colors removed); terminals lists them. problems lists VS Code's Problems panel (file, line, column, severity, message, errors first); find-in-files finds text in the workspace's files, unsaved editors included, with the workspace's excludes.
never: That Jarvis runs a task or a command the person did not ask for, or sends one with confirmed: true before the person said yes.
That the person must restart VS Code or reload its window after installing the extension.
That the person must start VS Code with a flag or change a desktop setting.
A menu path, a key or a key combination as something Jarvis does.
Any tool other than computer.app and computer.open.
save-document, open-document or another LibreOffice verb: VS Code's own verbs are save-file and open-file.
